cards.surface: the face of the stone slab
cards.scene: a single slab of pale warm limestone fills the entire frame, seen straight on and flat, close enough that no edge of the slab is visible. the stone is old and softly veined with fine grey and umber marbling, faintly worn and chipped at a few points. a low raking warm light crosses the whole surface from one side. there is nothing else in the picture, no room, no objects, no background, only the stone.
cards.text_in: the firm name is deeply incised into that stone in large classical roman capitals across two lines, reading exactly: HOGAN AND CROWN LAW, cut wide and confident so it fills most of the width of the slab. between the two lines runs a long carved horizontal rule with tapered ends. below the name, incised much smaller, the line hoganandcrownlaw.com. around and between the lettering, carved into the same stone, are delicate embellishments: slender olive branches, small leaves and a few tight rosettes, all cut into the surface as relief, never drawn on it. every groove is bare uncoloured stone, taking its darkness only from the shadow that gathers inside the cut, with a hard bright edge along the side facing the light. no paint, no gilding, no colour of any kind inside any groove
